newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to restore mobile telephones in Karachi.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to restore mobile telephones in Karachi.

text.p: The Pakistani government has decided to end a 17-month-old ban on cellular telephone services in the southern province of Sindh, including its violence-prone capital Karachi, government sources said on Thursday.
They said the caretaker Sindh provincial cabinet decided on Wednesday to restore the services and sent its recommendation to the government of caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid.
"We are waiting for a notification," said Irfan Qureshi, a regional general manager of Paktel Ltd, a subsidiary of British firm Cable & Wireless Plc.
He told Reuters the services should be restored by early next week in Karachi and Hyderabad.

The government of Benazir Bhutto, dismissed as prime minister by the president on November 5, cut off mobile telephone links in Karachi and Hyderabad in July 1995 in an attempt to disrupt the communications of the militant ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM).
More than 2,000 people were killed in 1995 in violence in Karachi, most of them in the struggle between the security forces and the MQM. At least 375 people have died this year.

Pakistan's three cellular telephone companies, a pager company and three telephone booth card companies say they are ready to resume business in Karachi, which previously accounted for 40 percent of their revenue in Pakistan.
Qureshi said Paktel could resume its services at short notice. "All our infrastructure and staff is in place," he said.

The three mobile telephone firms -- Paktel; Pakistan Mobile Telecommunications, a joint venture of U.S.-based Motorola Inc and local Saif Telecom; and Pakcom Ltd, a subsidiary of Luxembourg's Millicom -- have invested a combined total of at least $160 million in Pakistan, industry sources say.

Javaid Feroze, a director at Pakistan's Telecard Ltd, a pay-card phone service, said it would take about two weeks to start fifty percent of his company's 935 telephone booths in Karachi. The rest need repair and maintenance.
Telecard sued the government on July 24 for 2.2 billion rupees ($54.7 million) in compensation for lost business in Karachi. Feroze said the government had not yet responded.
